profiles.name: 20-day momentum
profiles.idea: Follow each coin's 20-day direction. Crypto trends because buying attracts buying and leveraged traders are forced out in cascades.
profiles.other_side: Traders fading the move and leveraged positions closed by liquidation.
profiles.entry: Long when price is up more than 5% over 20 days and above its 100-candle average; short on the mirror image. Checked when each 4h candle closes.
profiles.take_profit: None. A trade is closed when the 20-day return turns or price crosses the average.
profiles.backtest: Profit factor 1.34 (2021-22), 1.57 (2023-24), 1.44 on unseen 2025-26, of which 1.09 before June 2026. About 28% of trades win.
profiles.caveat: Most of the 2025-26 profit came after June 2026, and mostly from longs in rising markets.
profiles.rule: Keep if average R is above 0 and above the random-entry control after 30 closed trades. About 0.5 trades a day, so roughly two months.

profiles.name: Swing bot (20-day momentum under the desk Rules)
profiles.idea: Follow each coin's 20-day direction. Crypto trends because buying attracts buying and leveraged traders are forced out in cascades.
profiles.other_side: Traders fading the move and leveraged positions closed by liquidation.
profiles.entry: Long when price is up more than 5% over 20 days and above its 100-candle average; short on the mirror image. Checked when each 4h candle closes.
profiles.take_profit: None. A trade is closed when the 20-day return turns or price crosses the average.
profiles.backtest: Profit factor 1.34 (2021-22), 1.57 (2023-24), 1.44 on unseen 2025-26, of which 1.09 before June 2026. About 28% of trades win.
profiles.caveat: Same rule as the baseline, but it follows the desk Rules (risk %, trade limit, daily stops) and its own pauses, so it is not a like-for-like test. Counted from 2026-11-19.
profiles.rule: Not judged here. Compare it with the baseline to see what the desk Rules cost or save.

profiles.name: Daily momentum
profiles.idea: The same trend effect on a slower clock: fewer trades, lower cost per trade, less noise.
profiles.other_side: The same as the 4h bot: faders and forced sellers.
profiles.entry: Long when the 30-day return is positive and price is above its 50-day average; short on the mirror image. Checked once a day at 00:00 UTC.
profiles.take_profit: None. Closed when price crosses the 50-day average.
profiles.backtest: Profit factor 3.45 (2021-22), 1.65 (2023-24) and 1.63 on unseen 2025-26. About 0.2 trades a day, held three weeks on average; about 30% of trades win.
profiles.caveat: 2021-22 is flattered by one very large trend year. Most profit came from longs.
profiles.rule: Too slow to judge in a month. Keep if average R is above 0 after 20 closed trades; until then only check that it trades as its backtest does.

profiles.name: Relative strength, long and short
profiles.idea: Rank the six coins by 30-day return, hold the two strongest long and the two weakest short. It earns from the gap between strong and weak coins, so it does not need the market to rise or fall.
profiles.other_side: Holders slow to rotate out of lagging coins, and buyers of 'cheap' laggards.
profiles.entry: Each day at 00:00 UTC: long a coin ranked 1 or 2, short a coin ranked 5 or 6.
profiles.take_profit: None. Closed when the coin leaves the top three (longs) or bottom three (shorts).
profiles.backtest: Profit factor 1.22 (2021-22, drawdown 4%) and 1.35 (2023-24, drawdown 11%), about 0.25 trades a day, 44% of trades win. Not run on 2025-26. With six coins the ranking is coarse.
profiles.caveat: Shorts lost in 2023-24 (-18% against +38% from longs), so it was not market-neutral in practice. Its profit factors (1.22, 1.35) are only just above what random entries reached (up to 1.16), so the backtest evidence is weak.
profiles.rule: Keep if average R is above 0 after 20 closed trades and its weekly results do not simply copy the momentum profiles.

profiles.name: Momentum with a funding crowding filter
profiles.idea: The 20-day momentum rule, but no new longs while the coin's 7-day funding is in the top fifth of its last 90 days (longs are crowded), and no new shorts while it is in the bottom fifth.
profiles.other_side: Late, leveraged trend-followers who enter when the trade is already crowded.
profiles.entry: As 20-day momentum, plus the funding condition above.
profiles.backtest: Profit factor 1.28 (2021-22) and 1.61 (2023-24), against 1.34 and 1.57 for plain momentum with about 15% more trades. The filter made no measurable difference.
profiles.caveat: Kept as a side-by-side test against the baseline, not because the backtest favours it.
profiles.rule: Drop unless its average R beats the baseline's by a clear margin after 30 closed trades each.

profiles.name: Scalp: zone touch plus delta flip
profiles.idea: Enter when price touches one of your zones and a candle closes back out of it on heavy net buying (selling for a short).
profiles.other_side: Unclear. No one is obviously forced to trade here, which is the weakness.
profiles.entry: Market order at the close of the signal candle (timeframe and trigger are set on the Automation page).
profiles.take_profit: Thirds at 1R, 2R and 3R; stop to entry after the first.
profiles.backtest: 0 of 192 variants per timeframe made money after fees; the best 15m variant averaged -0.04 R. With limit-order entries, 0 of 384 on 5m and 15m (best 15m -0.05 R).
profiles.caveat: Every scalp idea tested so far lost after fees. This runs as a forward check of that result.
profiles.rule: The bot switches itself off after 200 closed trades if the total is negative.

profiles.name: Against the crowd (long/short account ratio)
profiles.idea: Binance publishes how many futures accounts are net long against net short. When that ratio is extreme for the coin, trade against it: small accounts crowd into the losing side and are the ones forced out.
profiles.other_side: The crowd of small accounts, late and leveraged on one side.
profiles.entry: Each hour: long when the ratio is in the lowest 5% of the coin's last 90 days (unusually few accounts long), short when in the highest 5%.
profiles.backtest: Profit factor 1.43 (Dec 2021 to Sep 2023) and 1.32 (to Jun 2025), about 1.1 trades a day, half of trades win. On the held-back period (Jul 2025 to Nov 2026) 1.15, while five random-entry runs gave 0.79 to 0.90. Daily results were unrelated to the momentum bot's (correlation 0.07).
profiles.caveat: The held-back result (1.15) is well below training and all of it came from shorts; drawdown there was 20%. The ratio is currently at regime highs for BTC and ETH (in the top 5% on about half of recent hours), so it will mostly be short. The live feed keeps its own 130-day history in lab/ratio.
profiles.rule: Keep if average R is above 0 and above the random-entry control after 60 closed trades. About one trade a day, so roughly two months.

profiles.name: Random entries
profiles.idea: No idea at all: random longs and shorts with the momentum bot's stop, closed after five days. It shows what luck looks like over the same weeks.
profiles.other_side: Nobody. Expected result is slightly below zero (fees).
profiles.entry: A random 2% of 4h candles long and 2% short, per coin.
profiles.backtest: Five different random sequences gave profit factors from 0.79 to 1.16 over 2021-22 and 2023-24 (about 410 trades each). That spread is what luck alone produces.
profiles.caveat: A backtest profit factor below about 1.2 on a few hundred trades is inside this luck band.
profiles.rule: Never promoted. A strategy that cannot beat this profile over the same period has shown nothing.
